sourcedFrom: 88™ AND 91™ PUMP-ACTION SHOTGUNS — Maverick Arms owner's manual — Part No. 67652, typeset 3/8/18 (2018 (typesetting stamp 3/8/18 on every page; no separate copyright line is printed))
cleanIntro: The 88 comes apart on its take-down screw — not a magazine cap — so the magazine spring stays captive in a closed tube the whole time. Empty it through the ejection port and then through the cartridge stop, park the bolt mid-port, back the screw out, and the barrel, trigger housing and receiver internals follow in that order.

steps.title: Safety fully RIGHT, and nothing near the trigger
steps.action: Push the safety button fully to the right to ON — on this gun the safe direction for the button is right, not rearward as on the tang-safety Mossbergs. Keep the muzzle pointed somewhere harmless and your fingers off the trigger for the whole unload; you are about to cycle the action several times.
steps.quote: Move the safety button (Fig. 2), fully to the right, to the “ON” (SAFE) position.
steps.cite: 88™ AND 91™ PUMP-ACTION SHOTGUNS — Maverick Arms owner's manual — Part No. 67652, typeset 3/8/18 — UNLOADING, p.7

steps.title: Chamber first — ease the shell out, don't launch it
steps.action: Press the action lock lever and draw the forearm back SLOWLY until the chambered shell is fully withdrawn and sitting visible in the ejection port, then lift it out by hand. Racking it briskly throws a live shell across the room; slow is the instruction and it is the whole difference.
steps.quote: Depress the action lock lever (Fig. 3) and pull the forearm rearward, slowly, until the live shotshell is completely withdrawn and visible in the ejection port.
steps.cite: 88™ AND 91™ PUMP-ACTION SHOTGUNS — Maverick Arms owner's manual — Part No. 67652, typeset 3/8/18 — UNLOADING, p.7

steps.title: Magazine tube through the cartridge stop, one at a time
steps.action: Close the bolt on an empty chamber, turn the gun trigger-guard-up, and put your thumb into the opening in the bottom of the receiver to depress the cartridge stop on the right side. Each press releases one shell off the tube. Keep going until nothing more comes; the tube is the place people leave a round.
steps.aside: Repeat until all shotshells are removed from the magazine tube.
steps.quote: Insert your right thumb into the opening in the bottom of the receiver and depress the cartridge stop on the right side to release shotshells one at a time (Fig. 9).
steps.cite: 88™ AND 91™ PUMP-ACTION SHOTGUNS — Maverick Arms owner's manual — Part No. 67652, typeset 3/8/18 — UNLOADING, p.7

steps.title: Action open, safety on, and glasses before anything moves
steps.action: Leave the action open and the safety ON, then look and feel in the chamber, the elevator and the magazine tube one more time. Eye protection goes on now: there are sprung parts in the receiver and solvent later, and this is the point of no return for both.
steps.aside: Wear eye protection during disassembly and cleaning.
steps.quote: Leave the action in the open, rearward position and the safety button in the “ON” (SAFE) position.
steps.cite: 88™ AND 91™ PUMP-ACTION SHOTGUNS — Maverick Arms owner's manual — Part No. 67652, typeset 3/8/18 — UNLOADING, p.7

steps.title: Bolt parked mid-port before the screw comes out
steps.action: Run the forearm fully back with the action lock lever pressed, then bring it slowly forward until the front of the bolt sits in the MIDDLE of the ejection port. That position is what lines the bolt slide up with the clearance cuts later — go fully forward and the internals will not come out without a fight.
steps.aside: Depress the action lock lever (Fig. 3) and open the action by sliding the forearm fully rearward.
steps.quote: Move the forearm slowly forward from the fully rearward position until the front of the bolt is in the middle of the ejection port (Fig. 7).
steps.cite: 88™ AND 91™ PUMP-ACTION SHOTGUNS — Maverick Arms owner's manual — Part No. 67652, typeset 3/8/18 — DISASSEMBLY / BARREL REMOVAL, p.7

steps.title: TAKE-DOWN SCREW, counterclockwise, all the way out of the tube
steps.action: An 88 comes apart on a take-down screw at the end of the magazine tube — turn it counterclockwise until its threads are completely clear of the tube end. Maverick prints the 88's screw and the 91's magazine cap in the same sentence: yours is the screw, and the 91's warning about a spring retainer under pressure is not this gun. The screw is captive in the forearm cap, so it stays with the parts rather than rolling away.
steps.quote: Loosen the 88™ Model “take down screw”, or 91™ Model “magazine cap”, by turning counterclockwise until the screw  threads are completely disengaged from the end of the magazine tube (Fig. 7).
steps.cite: 88™ AND 91™ PUMP-ACTION SHOTGUNS — Maverick Arms owner's manual — Part No. 67652, typeset 3/8/18 — DISASSEMBLY / BARREL REMOVAL, p.7

steps.title: Barrel out with a rocking pull, never a straight yank
steps.action: Work the barrel out of the receiver with a gentle back-and-forth twist while pulling. The barrel extension sits in a cut in the receiver and a dead-straight pull binds it; a small rotation frees it without scoring either part. Once it is off, do not close the action or touch the trigger — Maverick warns that doing either with the barrel off can damage the gun.
steps.aside: Never close the action or pull trigger while barrel is removed as damage could result to the firearm.
steps.quote: Remove the barrel from the receiver with a gentle back-and-forth rotational movement while pulling the barrel out of the receiver assembly.
steps.cite: 88™ AND 91™ PUMP-ACTION SHOTGUNS — Maverick Arms owner's manual — Part No. 67652, typeset 3/8/18 — DISASSEMBLY / BARREL REMOVAL, p.7

steps.title: One retainer pin drops the trigger housing
steps.action: Lay the gun down trigger-guard-up and drift out the small trigger housing retainer pin in the side of the receiver, about half an inch below the rear of the trigger guard. Maverick sets a maximum punch diameter of 3/16 inch — anything fatter does not fit the hole and swells the receiver around it.
steps.aside: Position the shotgun on a clean surface with the trigger guard upward.
steps.quote: push out the small diameter trigger housing retainer pin located on the side of the receiver, approximately a 1/2” (12.7 mm) below the rear of the trigger guard (Fig. 8)
steps.cite: 88™ AND 91™ PUMP-ACTION SHOTGUNS — Maverick Arms owner's manual — Part No. 67652, typeset 3/8/18 — TRIGGER HOUSING REMOVAL, p.8

steps.title: Housing out rear-first — and leave the trigger alone
steps.action: Lift the REAR of the trigger housing first and the assembly comes out of the receiver. Once it is out, do not pull the trigger: dropping the hammer with the housing unsupported damages the assembly and can catch a finger. The housing itself is not opened by an owner at any point.
steps.aside: The trigger housing is a complex assembly and must not be disassembled.
steps.quote: Remove the trigger housing assembly by lifting the rear portion upward first.
steps.cite: 88™ AND 91™ PUMP-ACTION SHOTGUNS — Maverick Arms owner's manual — Part No. 67652, typeset 3/8/18 — TRIGGER HOUSING REMOVAL, p.8

steps.title: Look before you go further — then cartridge stop and interrupter
steps.action: Take thirty seconds to study how the bolt, bolt slide and action slide bars sit together before you disturb them; they must go back in exactly that relationship. Then take the cartridge interrupter out of the ejection-port side and the cartridge stop out of the other. A light tap on the receiver sides releases them if they stick.
steps.aside: CAUTION: Before performing any further disassembly, take time to study how the in-
steps.quote: Remove the cartridge interrupter from the ejection port side and cartridge stop from the opposite side.
steps.cite: 88™ AND 91™ PUMP-ACTION SHOTGUNS — Maverick Arms owner's manual — Part No. 67652, typeset 3/8/18 — DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS, p.9

steps.title: Bolt slide up and out at the clearance cuts
steps.action: Move the forearm back until the bolt and bolt slide are about three quarters rearward, watching for the moment the bottom of the bolt slide lines up with the clearance cuts in the receiver walls — that is the only position it lifts out at. Forcing it anywhere else marks the receiver.
steps.quote: When the bottom of the bolt slide is aligned with the clearance cuts in the sides of the receiver, lift the bolt slide upward and out of the receiver (Fig. 10).
steps.cite: 88™ AND 91™ PUMP-ACTION SHOTGUNS — Maverick Arms owner's manual — Part No. 67652, typeset 3/8/18 — DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS, p.9

steps.title: Bolt forward and out through the barrel opening
steps.action: Slide the bolt assembly forward and out through the front of the receiver, the way the barrel went. It will not come out of the ejection port and trying is how the port lip gets burred.
steps.quote: Remove the bolt assembly by sliding it forward and out of the receiver assembly through the barrel opening at the front of the receiver (Fig. 11-A).
steps.cite: 88™ AND 91™ PUMP-ACTION SHOTGUNS — Maverick Arms owner's manual — Part No. 67652, typeset 3/8/18 — DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS, p.9

steps.title: Elevator pivoted up and squeezed out, then the forearm off
steps.action: Pivot the front of the elevator up out of the receiver, then squeeze its two arms together just enough to disengage its buttons from the receiver holes and lift it clear — squeeze only as far as it needs, the arms are sprung steel. Then the forearm and action slide assembly slides forward off the magazine tube and the strip is done.
steps.aside: Pivot the front portion of the elevator upward out of the receiver (Fig. 11-B).
steps.quote: Remove the forearm/action slide assembly by sliding it forward and off the magazine tube.
steps.cite: 88™ AND 91™ PUMP-ACTION SHOTGUNS — Maverick Arms owner's manual — Part No. 67652, typeset 3/8/18 — DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS, p.10

steps.title: Field strip complete — Maverick stops here
steps.action: Barrel, trigger housing, cartridge stop and interrupter, bolt slide, bolt, elevator, forearm. That is the whole published teardown, and the book closes it with an exclamation mark and a caution: nothing deeper belongs to routine cleaning, and the bolt and trigger housing are cleaned as complete assemblies.
steps.aside: Clean as complete assemblies with gun solvent and lightly lubricate with gun oil.
steps.cite: 88™ AND 91™ PUMP-ACTION SHOTGUNS — Maverick Arms owner's manual — Part No. 67652, typeset 3/8/18 — DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS, p.10

deepAbsentReason: Maverick publishes one teardown and it ends where the steps above end. The book's own words are "Field disassembly is now complete! The shotgun should not be disassembled further for routine cleaning or maintenance", and it separately states that the bolt and trigger housing are complex assemblies to be cleaned WHOLE and opened only by a Product Service Center or a qualified gunsmith. There is no deeper published procedure for an owner, so the absence is recorded rather than filled.

cleaning.name: BARREL & CHAMBER
tasks: Scrub bore and chamber with solvent, then patch until the patches come out clean
Finish with a lightly oiled patch for a protective film
Clean and remove any deposits in the barrel extension — that is where it binds

cleaning.name: BOLT & TRIGGER HOUSING (as assemblies)
tasks: Clean both as complete assemblies with gun solvent — neither is opened
Light gun oil afterwards, wiped rather than left wet

cleaning.name: RECEIVER & ACTION
tasks: Wipe residue out of the receiver, the bolt slide track and the action slide bars
Keep the bolt, bolt slide and slide bars in their relationship for reassembly
Very little oil — a light film on external surfaces is what this book asks for

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: Light oil on metal; avoid abrasives that mark the finish
Camo guns: keep strong solvents off the pattern
Store clean and oiled, never in a fabric-lined case that draws the oil out

reassembly: Receiver on a clean surface with the trigger housing opening upward.
Forearm assembly onto the magazine tube, guiding the action slide bars into their cuts in the front of the receiver.
Elevator arms squeezed together and its buttons seated in the 1/4 inch holes in the receiver, then pivoted so its forward portion is even with the edge of the cavity.
Bolt in through the barrel opening, bolt lock down and forward; depress the ejector so the bolt runs fully rearward — the ejector MUST land in its slot in the bolt.
Action bars set with the notch even with the cuts in the receiver wall; bolt slide slotted-side up, notch to the rear, front lowered first into the bolt lock cut.
Hold the bolt slide down and pull the forearm forward — everything should move freely. If it does not, DO NOT FORCE: take it apart and re-seat it.
Cartridge stop and cartridge interrupter back on the inside receiver walls, hooks facing inward toward the centre.
Hammer fully cocked, then the trigger housing lugs into the receiver slots, the rear eased down, and the retainer pin pushed in flush.
Barrel back in, then the take-down screw threaded into the magazine tube and tightened.
fncheck: Empty, muzzle safe, safety fully right to ON. Hold the action lock lever down and work the action open and closed several times — it should run free. Close it (forearm fully forward), leave the safety ON and pull the trigger fully: the hammer must not fall. Finger off, safety to OFF: still no fall. Safety OFF and trigger pulled: the hammer should fall. Finish with the action open and the safety back ON. Anything else and it goes to the Product Service Center rather than the field.
